                    COMPLAINT FOR PRELIIMINARY INJUNCITON, DECLARATORY JUDGMENT AND

                                           JURY TRIAL DEMAND







                                                  I.      INTRODUCTION

                           The Plaintiff, Holly Mayfield, Esq., is seeking equitable relief through this petition for



                  preliminary injunction and declaratory judgment as described below. This complaint alleges that



                  Defendant, Newrez, LLC, d/b/a Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing ("Shellpoint"), breached the



                  terms of that certain mortgage noted herein, given by the Defendant, Joseph Reardon, former



                  spouse of the Plaintiff as secured by the real property owned by the Plaintiff and Joseph Reardon



                  located at 4 Olde Logging Road, Marion, Massachusetts. The Defendants breached the mortgage



                  contract by sending a purported default notice in accordance with the mortgage contract that



                  failed to strictly comply with the condition precedent terms of Paragraph 22 of the Mortgage.



                  Plaintiff alleges that the default/right to cure notice described in this Complaint that was sent by



                  Defendant Shellpoint is invalid and resulted in a void acceleration and void foreclosure initiation



                  for a failure to strictly comply with a condition precedent of the mortgage, violating M.G.L. Ch

                  183 Section 21 and M.G.L. c. 244, Section 14.



                           Defendant's breach resulted in a void default notice pursuant to the terms to the mortgage



                  and a void acceleration of the mortgage pursuant to said mortgage.



                           Additionally, this complaint alleges that Defendant, Newrez, LLC, d/b/a Shellpoint



                  Mortgage Servicing ("Shellpoint") does not have the authority to accelerate the Mortgage and



                  invoke the Statutory Power of Sale under M. G. L. c. 183, § 21 and M. G. L. Ch. 244 § 14 on the



                  Plaintiff's real property located at 4 Olde Logging Road, Marion, Massachusetts (the "Property")



                  while the Defendant is not a “Lender” and does not hold the Promissory Note. Plaintiff avers



                  that the Defendant will not be able to convey said Property by "proper deed" in accordance with



                  the Massachusetts Statutory Power of Sale as set forth in M.G.L. c. 183, § 21 and M. G. L. Ch.



                  244 § 14 because the assignment of the Mortgage on the Property fails to show a consistent and



                  unbroken chain of title of the Mortgage and is therefore void and will not render a marketable



                  title as Newrez, LLC d/b/a Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing is not the holder of the Note and



                  therefore not capable of accelerating the Mortgage and/ or invoking the Statutory Power of Sale.



                  Accordingly, Plaintiffs are entitled to a declaratory judgment that Defendant lacked and lacks



                  standing to accelerate the Mortgage, foreclose and sell the Property, and that any foreclosures



                  and sale of the Property by Newrez, LLC, d/b/a Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing is ineffective,



                  without force or effect and void.



                           The Plaintiff prays that this Honorable Court find that the Defendant breached the terms



                  of the mortgage and further find said default notice and acceleration are invalid and void.



                  Further said Plaintiff also prays that this Honorable Court find that any foreclosure sale



                  conducted by the Defendant, Shellpoint, and foreclosure deed granted subsequent to the invalid



                  default notice be declared null and void regardless of whether or not said invalid foreclosure

                  deed was recorded, enjoin the Defendant, Shellpoint, from conducting any foreclosure auction



                  or conveyance of the subject property and declare any resulting foreclosure deed null and void.



                  Plaintiff also seeks declaratory relief, injunctive relief, actual, monetary, punitive and exemplary



                  damages, restitution, an accounting, attorney's fees and costs, and all other relief provided by law



                  for Defendant's wrongful acts.



                                                         JURISDICTION AND VENUE



                  1.       This Honorable Court has subject matter jurisdiction as the subject property at issue is



                  located in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, Plymouth County, and Plaintiff resides at said



                  subject property.



                  2.       Venue is proper in this Honorable Court in that the events or omissions giving rise to this



                  claim have occurred, and the real property that is subject of the action is situated within the



                  Commonwealth of Massachusetts, Plymouth County.



                                                                     PARTIES



                  3.       Plaintiff, Holly Mayfield, Esq., is a citizen of Massachusetts and the co-owner of the subject



                  property located at 4 Olde Logging Road, Marion, Massachusetts 02738.



                  4.       Defendant, Newrez, LLC, d/b/a Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing is a residential mortgage



                  servicing company, located at 75 Beattle Place, Suite 300, Greenville, SC 29601.



                  5.       Defendant, Joseph Reardon, is a citizen of Massachusetts and the co-owner of the subject



                  property located at 4 Olde Logging Road, Marion, Massachusetts 02738.







                                                    ALLEGATIONS OF THE PLAINTIFFS



                  6.       Plaintiff, Holly Mayfield, Esq., resides at and claims to be the co-owner of real property



                  located 4 Olde Logging Road, Marion, Massachusetts, which is the subject property as

                  7.       On January 2, 2019, the subject property was granted by quitclaim deed to the Defendant,



                  Joseph Reardon, Plaintiff's Husband. The Deed evidencing that conveyance of the subject property



                  was recorded in the Plymouth County Registry of Deeds on January 2, 2019, Book 50691, Page



                  107.



                  8.       On May 18, 2021, Defendant, Joseph Reardon, granted a mortgage secured by their



                  interest in the subject property, in the amount of $444,780.00, for the benefit of the the Plaintiff



                  and himself, which was recorded in the Plymouth County Registry of Deeds in Document No.



                  00057276 on May 18, 2021. (the Mortgage) The Mortgage identified “Nationstar Mortgage, LLC,



                  d/b/a Mr. Cooper” as the Lender and MERS as mortgagee.



                  9.       The Mortgage states at paragraph 22 as follows:



                               "22. Acceleration; Remedies. Lender shall give notice to Borrower prior to

                               acceleration following Borrower's breach of any covenant or agreement in this

                               Security Instrument ... The notice shall specify: (a) the default; (b) the action required

                               to cure the default; (c) a date, not less than 30 days from the date the notice is given to

                               Borrower, by which the default must be cured; and (d) that failure to cure the default

                               on or before the date specified in the notice may result in acceleration of the sums

                               secured by this Security Instrument and sale of the Property. The notice shall further

                               inform Borrower of the right to reinstate after acceleration and the right to bring a

                               court action to assert the non-existence of a default or any other defense of Borrower

                               to acceleration and sale. If the default is not cured on or before the date specified in

                               the notice, Lender at its option may require immediate payment in full of all sums

                               secured by this Security Instrument without further demand and may invoke the

                               STATUTORY POWER OF SALE and any other remedies permitted by Applicable

                               Law. Lender shall be entitled to collect all expenses incurred in pursuing the remedies

                               provided in this Section 22, including, but not limited to, reasonable attorneys' fees

                               and costs of title evidence.



                               If Lender invokes the STATUTORY POWER OF SALE, Lender shall mail a copy of

                               a notice of sale to Borrower and to other persons prescribed by Applicable Law, in

                               the manner provided by Applicable Law. Lender shall publish the notice of sale, and

                               the Property shall be sold in the manner prescribed by Applicable Law. Lender or its

                               designee may purchase the Property at any sale. The proceeds of the sale shall be

                               applied in the following order: (a) to all expenses of the sale, including, but not

                               limited to, reasonable attorneys' fees; (b) to all sums secured by this Security

                               Instrument; and (c) any excess to the person or persons legally entitled to it."





                  10.      The Mortgage states at paragraph 15 as follows: "any notice to borrower...shall be



                  deemed to have been given to Borrower when mailed by first class mail or when actually



                  delivered to Borrower's notice address if sent by other means".



                  11.      Paragraph 19 of the Mortgage also required that prior to acceleration and foreclosure the



                  Defendant was required to send the “borrowers” a Default Notice which informed the Plaintiff



                  and Defendant Joseph Reardon (the “borrowers”)           that they had a "right to reinstate after



                  acceleration".



                  12.      On February 14, 2025, the Mortgage was purportedly assigned from MERS to the



                  Defendant Newrez, LLC, d/b/a Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing. Said assignment was recorded in



                  the Plymouth County Registry of Deeds in Document No. 00009274 on February 14, 2025.



                  13.      The grantor of the assignment recorded on February 15, 2025 is not the same named



                  entity as the grantee of the promissory note (“the Note”), which was granted to the actual Lender,



                  “Nationstar Mortgage, LLC, d/b/a Mr. Cooper”. The Defendant, Newrez, LLC, d/b/a Shellpoint



                  Mortgage Servicing is not a “Lender” where it does not hold the Note and there is no evidence



                  that the Note was duly transferred or assigned to the Defendant Shellpoint.            Therefore,



                  Defendant, Shellpoint is barred from asserting the authority to foreclose the mortgage on behalf



                  of the Lender, “Nationstar LLC, d/b/a Mr. Cooper”. Notice of any such transfer of interest or



                  authority purportedly held by the Defendant, Shellpoint, was not duly provided and not



                  contained within the complete record for the mortgage acquired by subpoena to the Plaintiff.



                  See, Eaton v. Nat'l Mort. Ass'n, 462 Mass. 569 (2012).



                  14.      Plaintiff avers that the Defendant, Shellpoint, did not send and that Plaintiff did not

                  receive any Default Notice or Acceleration Notice in accordance with Paragraph 22 of the



                  Mortgage.



                  15.      Plaintiff further alleges that any notice purportedly sent by the Defendant, Shellpoint, was



                  sent only to the Defendant, Joseph Reardon, residing at a different address, purporting to state compliance



                  with paragraph 22 of the Mortgage and failed to contain the required information as described in



                  the Mortgage and was not in strict compliance with said paragraph.



                  16.      The Defendants accelerated the mortgage. The acceleration is null and void.



                  17.      On November 26, 2025, Defendants caused to be filed a Complaint in the Massachusetts



                  Land Court pursuant to the Servicemembers Relief Act 50 USC c. 50 § 3901 et. seq. to



                  determine Servicemember status of the Defendant, Joseph Reardon, for the purpose of initiating



                  foreclosure action against Plaintiff and Mr. Reardon. The action was assigned docket no.



                  25SM003706.



                  18.      On November 26, 2025, Defendant, Shellpoint, filed in the Land Court Case a Mortgagee's



                  Affidavit Under Chapter 206 of the Acts of 2007, purporting to act on behalf of the “holder of



                  the note”. The Affidavit was signed under the pains and penalties of perjury by the Defendant



                  Shellpoint, and stated that the Defendant, Joseph Reardon, was sent a notice dated January 16,



                  2025 pursuant to the 90 Day Right to Cure Default under M.G.L. c. 244 § 35A.



                  19.      On November 26, 2025, Defendant, Shellpoint, filed a Complaint to Determine Military



                  Status, in which it states that it “alleges on information and belief that the Defendant(s) is/are the



                  only person(s) holding the equity of redemption of the property covered by the mortgage



                  described in paragraph 1 of this Complaint so far as it appears of record in the said Registry of



                  Deeds and as known to your Plaintiff”.



                  20.      On January 2, 2019, the Defendant executed a Homestead in the name of the Plaintiff,

                  Holly Mayfield, as Wife, recorded in the Plymouth County Registry of Deeds as Document No.

                  21.      On September 3, 2024, the Plaintiff and the Defendant, Joseph Reardon, executed a



                  Judgment of Divorce entered in the Plymouth County Probate and Family Court on September



                  12, 2024. Page 15 of the Judgment of Divorce grants the equity in the property (the former



                  marital home) solely to the Plaintiff and orders the Defendant, Joseph Reardon to execute a deed



                  to Plaintiff, granting her sole title and interest in the property.



                  22.      On or about January 30, 2025, Plaintiff contacted the Defendant, Shellpoint, and gave



                  notice of her interest in the property and inquired as to the procedure by which she could obtain



                  an assumption of the mortgage, wherefore, she believed the Defendant, Joseph Reardon had



                  defaulted on the mortgage.



                  23.      On or about May 1, 2025, the Plaintiff requested all records relating to the mortgage and



                  note from the Defendant, Shellpoint, by formal subpoena under the pending post-judgment



                  litigation in the divorce.



                  24.      Included in the subpoena response are records of the correspondence between the



                  Defendants between September of 2024 and May of 2025, regarding Plaintiff's successor



                  interest, with demands by Defendant, Joseph Reardon that the Defendant, Shellpoint, refrain



                  from providing any information to the Plaintiff about the mortgage.



                  25.      The Defendant, Shellpoint, had actual knowledge of the Plaintiff's successor interest in



                  the property, and failed to provide any due notice as required by M.G.L. c. 244, Section 14, and



                  furthermore, reported knowingly false information in its Land Court Complaint purporting to



                  know of no other person holding the equity of redemption of the property.



                  25.      By the terms of the Judgment of Divorce, entered in the Probate and Family Court on

                  September 12, 2024, the Plaintiff is the holder of a successor interest and Defendant, Joseph



                  Reardon was required to execute a deed to the property to the Plaintiff.



                  26.      The Plaintiff intended to sell the property, which has been actively listed for sale since



                  October of 2024. However, the said Judgment of Divorce was appealed and is presently pending



                  in the Court of Appeals (Appeals Court Docket No. 2025-P-1147; 2025-P-0822; and Supreme



                  Judicial Court Docket No. SJ-2025-0493). The Plaintiff and the Defendant, Joseph Reardon are



                  precluded from taking further action towards resolution of the outstanding mortgage due to the



                  appeal. Once decided in the Court of Appeals, new orders will be required from the probate and



                  family court, resolving the issues presented by this action, rendering Defendant, Shellpoint's,



                  exercise of its power of sale moot.



                  27.      Plaintiff is an innocent party to the foreclosure, whose rights are affected by the



                  misconduct of the Defendants. Plaintiff is at risk of imminent irreparable harm to her interests



                  by the Defendant's actions.    Plaintiff's likelihood of success on the merits is guaranteed. Both



                  the Plaintiff, and the Defendant, Joseph Reardon have and continue to make reasonable efforts to



                  sell the property, but are precluded by the delay of the probate and family court proceedings.



                  28.      Plaintiff was entitled to due notice as required by M.G.L. c. 244, Section 14, as she is, by



                  definition, a “person of record...holding an interest in the property...” and has an unequivocal



                  right to reinstate the mortgage before the foreclosure.



                  29.      Furthermore, the default/right to cure notice states on page 4 that "You may redeem the



                  property by paying the total amount due prior to the foreclosure sale" and that Shellpoint



                  "reserves the right to accept or reject a partial payment of the total amount due without waving



                  its right to proceed with foreclosure".     Since the "total amount due" when the mortgage is



                  accelerated is the accelerated amount, this language is contrary to, waters down and infringes

                  upon the unequivocal right to reinstate the mortgage by paying less the accelerated amount



                  "anytime" before the foreclosure. The above statements are additional and unnecessary language



                  in the notice that is not in strict compliance with the mortgage because it may serve to water



                  down, contradict or nullify the Plaintiff's unequivocal right to reinstate their mortgages and to



                  "still avoid foreclosure by paying the total past due amount before a foreclosure sale takes place".



                  See Fed. Nat'l Mortg. Ass'n v. Marroquin, 74 N.E.3d 592 (Mass. 2017).



                  30.      Plaintiff alleges that the purported Default Notice sent by the Defendants failed to fully



                  and "properly" describe the mortgagor's "right to reinstate after acceleration" as required by and



                  detailed in Paragraph 22 of the Mortgage. Furthermore, the form notice's statement that



                  "Shellpoint "reserves the right to accept or reject a partial payment of the total amount due



                  without waving its right to proceed with foreclosure" is additional and unnecessary language in



                  the notice that is not in strict compliance with the mortgage because it may serve to water down,



                  contradict or nullify the mortgagor's unequivocal right to reinstate the mortgage and to "still



                  avoid foreclosure by paying the total past due amount before a foreclosure sale takes place".



                  31.      The Defendants' notice is in breach of the strict compliance standard of the mortgage, the



                  condition precedent to accelerate the Mortgage and a violation of the Statutory Power of Sale



                  pursuant to M.G.L. ch. 183 §21 for failing to provide a "proper" default notice in accordance



                  with Paragraph 22 of the Mortgage as a condition precedent to foreclosure.



                  32.      As such, the Defendant failed to provide the Plaintiff and the Defendant, Joseph Reardon



                  proper Notice of Default in breach of the Mortgage contract for failure to first comply with the



                  terms of the mortgage prior to exercising the power of sale, rendering any acceleration,



                  foreclosure, and sale void.

                                                       COUNT I

                               BREACH OF CONTRACT AND FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH CONDITIONS

                                              PRECEDENT TO ACCELERATION



                  33.      Plaintiff repeats and re-alleges every allegation above as if set forth herein in full.



                  34.      As described above, the mortgage contract entered into by Defendant, Joseph Reardon and



                  former lender, “Nationstar, LLC, d/b/a Mr. Cooper” constitutes a valid offer.



                  35.      Upon Defendant, Joseph Reardon executing the mortgage contract and giving it to the



                  Lender, the Lender accepted that offer.



                  36.      Alternatively, Defendant, Joseph Reardon's execution of the mortgage contract thereby



                  purporting to give his security interest in the property to the Lender constitutes an offer.



                  Acceptance of the offer occurred when Defendants accepted payments made by Mr. Reardon



                  pursuant to the mortgage contract.



                  37.      The mortgage contract was supported by consideration. Defendant, Joseph Reardon's



                  payments to Defendant, Shellpoint, constitutes consideration.



                  38.      Defendant, Shellpoint, and Defendant, Joseph Reardon thereby formed a valid contract



                  and Plaintiff was and remains ready, willing and able to perform as successor in interest under



                  said contract.



                  39.      Defendant, Shellpoint, breached the mortgage contract by failing to meet its obligations



                  pursuant to, the terms as agreed to found at paragraphs 15 and 22 of the Mortgage which state in



                  pertinent part, at paragraph 22 as follows:



                                "22. Acceleration; Remedies. Lender shall give notice to Borrower prior to

                                acceleration following Borrower's breach of any covenant or agreement in this

                                Security Instrument ... The notice shall specify: (a) the default; (b) the action required

                                to cure the default; (c) a date, not less than 30 days from the date the notice is given to

                                Borrower, by which the default must be cured; and (d) that failure to cure the default

                                on or before the date specified in the notice may result in acceleration of the sums

                                secured by this Security Instrument and sale of the Property. The notice shall further

                  40.      The Mortgage states at paragraph 15 as follows: "any notice to borrower. .. shall be



                  deemed to have been given to Borrower (and all other persons holding interest in the property)



                  when mailed by first class mail or when actually delivered to Borrower's notice address or “sent



                  by other means".



                  41.      Paragraph 22 of the Mortgage also provides that prior to acceleration and foreclosure, the



                  Defendant, Shellpoint, was required to send the borrowers (and holders of successive interest) a



                  Default Notice which informed borrowers that they had a "right to reinstate after acceleration".



                  42.          In Massachusetts, a contract containing an obligation of the Lender is construed as a



                  condition precedent, which requires strict compliance.



                  43.          In Massachusetts, a mortgagee agreeing to abide certain obligations pursuant to the



                  mortgage before acceleration, foreclosure, and sale, must adhere to those obligations, with the



                  level of specificity as agreed.



                  44.      In Massachusetts, strict compliance with the requirements of paragraph 22 of the

Superior Court - Plymouth

                  mortgage is an obligation of the mortgagee. Failure to send proper Notice of Default pursuant to



                  paragraph 22 as noted herein and M.G.L. c. 244, Section 14, is a breach of mortgage contract



                  rendering any acceleration, attempted foreclosure, and sale of the subject property void.



                  45.      Plaintiff avers that the Defendant, Shellpoint, did not send, and that Plaintiff did not



                  receive any Default Notice or Acceleration Notice in accordance with Paragraph 22 of the



                  Mortgage.



                  46.      Plaintiffs further allege that any notice sent purporting to state compliance with paragraph



                  22 of the Mortgage failed to contain the required information as described in the Mortgage



                  and or contained additional information that was not in strict compliance with said paragraph.



                  47.      The Defendant, Shellpoint, accelerated the mortgage. The acceleration is null and void.



                  48.      On November 26, 2025, Defendant, Shellpoint, caused to be filed a Complaint in the



                  Massachusetts Land Court pursuant to the Servicemembers Relief Act 50 USC c. 50 § 3901 et.



                  seq. to determine Servicemember status of the Defendant, Joseph Reardon, for the purpose of



                  initiating foreclosure action. The action was assigned as docket no. 25SM003706.



                  49.      On November 26, 2025, Defendants filed in the Land Court Case a Mortgagee's Affidavit



                  Under Chapter 206 of the Acts of 2007. The Affidavit was signed under the pains and penalties



                  of perjury by the Defendant, Shellpoint, and stated that notice was sent in compliance with the



                  Mortgagor's 90 Day Right to Cure his Default under M.G.L. c. 244 § 35A.



                  50.      The Defendant, Shellpoint's, sworn affidavit in the Land Court Case appears to be a



                  "hybrid" form default/ right to cure Notice dated November 24, 2025 purporting to comply with



                  M.G.L c. 244 §35A.



                  51.          The Notice that was obtained through subpoena by the Plaintiff is dated January 16,



                  2025, and states that “After 4/16/2025, you can still avoid foreclosure by paying the total past due

                  amount before a foreclosure sale takes place”, and “If you do not pay the total past due amount of



                  $6,537.047 by 4/16/2025, you may be evicted from your home after a foreclosure sale". This language



                  effectively extended the Plaintiff and Defendant, Mr. Reardon's, right to reinstate after



                  acceleration to "anytime" before the foreclosure. See, Thompson v. JP Morgan Chase Bank, NA.,



                  486 Mass. 286 (2020).



                  52.      Contrary to the unequivocal right to reinstate that was extended to "anytime" before the



                  foreclosure, the default/right to cure notice states that "You may redeem the property by paying



                  the total amount due prior to the foreclosure sale" and that Shellpoint "reserves the right to



                  accept or reject a partial payment of the total amount due without waving its right to proceed



                  with foreclosure".



                  53.      Firstly, Plaintiff was not provided actual notice as required by statue, and was not then



                  able to intervene. Any rights of the Plaintiff to cure the default could not be duly asserted.



                  54.      Second, since the "total amount due" when the mortgage is accelerated is the accelerated



                  amount, this language is contrary to, waters down and infringes upon the Plaintiffs unequivocal



                  right to reinstate the mortgage by paying less the accelerated amount "anytime" before the



                  foreclosure.



                  55.      The above statements are additional and unnecessary language in the notice that is not in



                  strict compliance with the Plaintiffs' mortgage because it may serve to water down, contradict or



                  nullify the Plaintiffs' unequivocal right to reinstate their mortgages and to "still avoid foreclosure



                  may paying the total past due amount before a foreclosure sale takes place". See Fed. Nat'l



                  Mortg. Ass'n v. Marroquin, 74 N.E.3d 592 (Mass. 2017).



                  56.      Such ambiguous and unnecessary language in the hybrid notice as stated above presumes



                  to give the Defendant, Shellpoint, the power to delay acceptance of or reject a tender of payment

                  pursuant to the unequivocal right to reinstate under Paragraphs 19 and 22 of the Mortgage. Such

                  57.       Plaintiff alleges that the purported Default Notice filed in the Land Court case by the



                  Defendants failed to fully and "properly" describe the Plaintiffs' "right to reinstate after



                  acceleration" as required by and detailed in Paragraph 22 of the Mortgage. Furthermore, the



                  form notice's statement that "Shellpoint "reserves the right to accept or reject a partial payment

                  unnecessary language in the notice that is not in strict compliance with the mortgage because it



                  may serve to water down, contradict or nullify the unequivocal right to reinstate the mortgages



                  and to "still avoid foreclosure may paying the total past due amount before a foreclosure sale takes

                  58.       The Defendants' notice is in breach of the strict compliance standard of the mortgage, the



                  condition precedent to accelerate the Mortgage and a violation of the Statutory Power of Sale



                  pursuant to M.G.L. ch. 183 §21 for failing to provide a "proper" default notice in accordance



                  with Paragraph 22 of the Mortgage as a condition precedent to foreclosure.



                  59.       As such, the Defendant, Shellpoint, failed to provide the Plaintiff or Defendant, Mr.



                  Reardon, proper Notice of Default in breach of the Mortgage contract for failure to first comply



                  with the terms of the mortgage prior to exercising the power of sale, rendering any acceleration,



                  foreclosure, and sale void.



                  60.       Due to these failures to comply with the terms of the mortgage, no entity was

                  contractually authorized to accelerate the mortgage, exercise the statutory power of sale,

                  61.       As a result of the above noted improper and invalid exercises of the statutory power of



                  sale and purported foreclosure sale, the mortgage loan account was charged fees, costs and



                  expenses for certified mail, advertising costs, legal fees, auctioneer costs and other pending



                  charges.



                  62.       The Plaintiff has incurred damages in asserting her rights, in regard to the improper actions



                  of Defendant, Shellpoint, in seeking to accelerate without first complying with the terms of the



                  mortgage in violation of G. L. c. 183, § 21 and in breach of the contract.



                  63.       The Plaintiff has incurred fees for the prosecution of this action as a result of Defendants'



                  wrongful acceleration, premature charging of fees to Defendant, Joseph Rearsdon's account in



                  violation of G. L. c. 183, § 21 due to the breach of contract by Defendant, Shellpoint, as noted



                  herein.



                  64.       Plaintiff has suffered harm and is threatened with additional harm from Defendant's



                  breach, including but not limited to loss of property interests, higher principal loan balances,



                  emotional distress for fear of unlawful eviction; inappropriate fees and charges assessed to the



                  account, including broker price opinion fees, inspection fees, attorney's fees, "process



                  management" fees, late fees and other charges associated with delinquency and default, and



                  increased accrued interest.



                  65.       The Defendant, Shellpoint's, breach of contract and failure to comply with terms of the



                  mortgage as noted herein above, are the direct cause of the harm alleged herein and not Plaintiff's



                  or Defendant, Joseph Reardon's failure to make the mortgage payments.

                  66.      Therefore, Plaintiff would not have suffered acceleration, foreclosure sale, or the harms



                  as noted herein were it not for the Defendants breach of the mortgage contracts.
